definitions.explanation: The passing down of stories, knowledge, customs, or history by word of mouth rather than through written records. Also used as a suru verb meaning to hand down orally.

examples.japanese: この{物語|ものがたり}は{口承|こうしょう}で{伝|つた}えられてきた。
examples.english: This story has been passed down through oral tradition.

examples.japanese: {口承|こうしょう}{文学|ぶんがく}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}にある。
examples.english: Oral literature exists all over the world.

examples.japanese: {文字|もじ}を{持|も}たない{民族|みんぞく}の{歴史|れきし}は{口承|こうしょう}によって{受|う}け{継|つ}がれてきた。
examples.english: The history of peoples without a writing system has been carried on through oral tradition.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {口|こう} (mouth) + {承|しょう} (to receive, to carry on). Refers to the cultural practice of transmitting stories, songs, legends, and knowledge by word of mouth across generations. Common in anthropology, folklore studies, and literature.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {口承|こうしょう}{文学|ぶんがく} (oral literature)
- {口承|こうしょう}{文化|ぶんか} (oral culture)
- {口承|こうしょう}で{伝|つた}える (to pass down orally)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口伝|くでん}: oral instruction — emphasizes teaching or transmitting skills by word of mouth
- {言|い}い{伝|つた}え: legend, tradition — a specific story handed down, rather than the practice of oral transmission itself
